reuse.why: The API and existing consumers reuse getExpectedScheduleAmount, but its approximate calculation reimplements the existing getApproxNumberThreshold helper.

duplication.why: The rounded 7.5% tolerance formula duplicates shared/rules.ts, creating a second definition of a policy that matching and planning must share.

placement.why: Expected-amount selection remains in shared/schedules.ts, while API serialization stays in the existing schedule model.

scope.why: The edits focus on expected schedule amounts, their consumers, API exposure, and accompanying tests.

maintainability.why: Centralized selection is useful, but the duplicated tolerance, unused rounding parameter, and retained caller-side rounding selection leave unnecessary maintenance burdens.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts: getExpectedScheduleAmount calculates tolerance directly instead of calling getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: The tolerance formula is duplicated directly; it is not renamed or reshaped to conceal duplication.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount adds amountOp and an isapprox branch while retaining the now-unused _rounding parameter; callers still supply midpoint/template modes, including the obsolete selection in schedule-template.ts.
